items.fact: The campaign is split into five chapters, and PC Gamer counts 91 story missions in total.
Push Square and Insider Gaming both count 93 story missions across the five chapters. The count differs from PC Gamer's, which is probably because of optional missions.

The chapters are Just Like Paradise (Leonida Keys, 22 missions), Paradise Lost (Port Gellhorn, 11 plus 3 optional), Tits, Ass, Drug Money (Vice City, 26 plus 1 optional), Vice City, Baby (25), and Top of the World, Ma (7).
You follow Jason and Lucia through Leonida. Chapter 3 is the point where you can switch between the two.
Chapter 3 has you working for employers such as Dre'Quan Priest, Boobie Ike and Raul Bautista.
Leonida has six main regions: Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia and Mount Kalaga National Park.
There are 18 sets of collectible cards, and you can sell them at pawn shops. Random cards also turn up in yellow containers.
A completionist run requires finding all 100 basketball hoop locations in Leonida.
There are 40 unique race locations. Entering a race costs an entry fee plus a vehicle rental fee, but a win pays more than you put in.
Robberies are the fastest way to earn money. The Robberies section of the map index shows the potential score and key valuables for each gang hideout, Smash 'n' Grab, bank and Payday Loan location.
Moses, who you meet in Chapter 2, buys stolen cars without trackers for roughly $1,000 to $5,000 each. Randy, from Chapter 3, pays much more for high-end cars.
Randy's wish list has 18 high-end sports cars. Delivering one can pay $30,000 or more.
Bank vault robberies become available near the end of Chapter 4. They can pay up to $200,000 but need a lot of planning and equipment, and they trigger a 4-star wanted level.
Robbing rival gangs' hideouts is a strong late-game earner. The hideouts respawn and can pay $10,000 to $30,000 per run, and the big vault always comes back.
The Slim Jim you get in the Chapter 2 mission Moses lets you break into cars quietly. Before that, the only option is smashing the window, which draws attention.
Pay 'n' Spray shops buy cars but refuse any with a high-end tracker. They also cap sales at about three or four cars per day, and sleeping resets the cap.
Robberies at medium or high security locations are much easier as a pair. Hold off on most of them until you can play as both Jason and Lucia.
Skip banks and loan stores until you have a dye pack jammer, because the dye packs in their cash explode if you get too far from the building.
Buses and trains give you a cheap form of fast travel, but they run on a schedule so you have to wait for them.
Missions cannot be replayed once you complete them.
Two updates arrived before launch, 01.002.000 on Nov 13 and 01.002.001 on Nov 16, and Rockstar published no patch notes for either.
Some PS5 and Xbox players report crashes, including error CE-108255-1 at the start of the prologue or during the Pipework mission. Sony's support page says to update the game.
A glitch can force first-person mode even though the game doesn't officially support it, and once it's active you can't switch back to third-person.
A reported glitch on version 01.002.001 uncaps the frame rate above the usual 30 FPS lock. It was seen on an Xbox Series X connected to a 120Hz monitor.
